statement: You are given a non-negative integer n and an operation, which is either "set" or "unset".
For "set", turn the lowest-positioned 0 bit of n into a 1. The answer is n | (n + 1), because adding 1 turns that bit on and only clears 1 bits below it, which the OR puts back.

For "unset", turn the lowest-positioned 1 bit of n into a 0. The answer is n & (n − 1), because subtracting 1 turns that bit off and only sets 0 bits below it, which the AND removes. When n is 0 there is no 1 bit to clear and the result is 0.

examples.explanation: 12 is 1100. Its lowest 0 bit is bit 0, so the result is 1101: 12 | 13 = 13.
12 is 1100. Its lowest 1 bit is bit 2, so the result is 1000: 12 & 11 = 8.
